context_requirements: Functional voltage-gated sodium channels (e.g., SCN5A/SCN9A/SCN10A) or epithelial sodium channels (SCNN1A/B/G) must be expressed and electrically active.
A sodium-dependent, excitability-driven transcriptional program must be present; most immortalized adherent cancer lines lack this.
For any indirect effect, the drug must engage a sodium channel that couples to a signaling pathway (e.g., calcium influx, MAPK) in that lineage.
falsifiers: Reproducible, dose-dependent changes in landmark gene expression at 6 h or 24 h in any of the nine lines.
A shared transcriptional signature across multiple lines that matches known sodium-channel-blocker responses.
Evidence of SCN5A/SCN9A/SCN10A or SCNN1A/B/G expression and function in these lines coupled to gene expression changes.

evidence.supports: Sodium channel blockade can reverse injury-induced downregulation of a sodium channel gene in neurons, but this is a neuronal context not represented in the nine cancer lines.
A sodium channel blocker insecticide caused oxidative stress, inflammation and apoptosis in rat liver/kidney, but only at high in vivo doses and not via direct transcriptional targeting.
A charged sodium channel blocker (QX-314) modulated lung pathology in influenza-infected mice, an immune/neuronal context absent from the panel.
Indoxacarb, a sodium channel blocker insecticide, altered gene expression in silkworm midgut, but this is an insect toxicity response not expected in human cell lines.

A cysteine-rich protein with ion channel blocking activity suppressed proliferation and induced apoptosis in HeLa cells via Akt, suggesting possible indirect effects, but the agent is not a classical sodium channel blocker.
